This Curraweela fire is also linked to the later AGRN 1056 declaration; total burn area across the six main fires reached almost 9,000 ha.

summary: A wave of bushfires broke out across five central/northern NSW LGAs from mid-February 2023. Other fires near Currabubula and Blackville threatened but did not confirm home losses in the reports found.

Combined burn area across the 11-council declaration reached almost 48,000 ha.

The best-documented single fire, Willi Willi Road near Moparrabah (Kempsey), broke out of containment in Willi Willi National Park in mid-October, burned over 30,000 ha, destroyed four homes and two sheds, and killed a 56-year-old man who was trying to save his property near Temagog. The declaration also overlaps the Dthinna Dthinnawan and Nymboida/Tabulam fires covered under other AGRNs.

summary: The Coolagolite fire broke out on 3 October 2023 south of Bermagui on the NSW South Coast and, driven by winds up to 100 km/h, quickly reached Emergency Warning level, with residents in Cuttagee, Barragga Bay, Murrah, Bunga and Goalen Head told it was too late to leave. NSW RFS initially reported four homes destroyed but revised this to two homes destroyed and two damaged, plus 14 outbuildings destroyed and five damaged, over a fire ground that grew to almost 8,600 ha (an early estimate put it at 7,000 ha). One man was hospitalised during the emergency.

summary: This declaration covers a huge, multi-fire outbreak across the NSW/Queensland border region from mid-October 2023, ultimately burning over 132,000 ha, among the largest single declarations of the 2023 spring crisis. The Ogilvie Drive fire jumped the Clarence River and struck Tabulam, Donnybrook and Wallangarra at the end of October/early November; NSW RFS figures fluctuated during the emergency (peaking at 10 homes/23 outbuildings destroyed) before a later assessment confirmed four homes and 14 outbuildings destroyed, with almost 43,000 ha burned in the Tenterfield LGA alone. RFS volunteer Senior Deputy Captain John Holmes died of a medical episode while fighting fires near Kyogle during the same emergency.

The fire burned about 272 ha (later reported up to 781 ha) and at least one property was reported destroyed, with further losses feared at the height of the emergency; no final confirmed toll was found in this search.

summary: The Duck Creek fire broke out in Pilliga State Forest, 18 km south of Narrabri, around 8 December 2023 and became one of the largest and most dramatic fires of the season, generating a pyrocumulonimbus thunderstorm on 18-19 December and growing from about 112,000 ha to a final size of roughly 143,000 ha. Residents were escalated from evacuation to 'too late to leave/shelter' warnings, and evacuation centres opened in Coonabarabran, Gunnedah and Narrabri; as of 21 December no homes had been confirmed lost, though the active fireground initially prevented full building assessments. Ash reportedly reached Dubbo (200 km away) and smoke haze reached Sydney.
